mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes recession and reduced corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong demand growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 6% signals a breakout in inflation, which increases the likelihood of aggressive central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6% in one month (vs previous month)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of stable monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical artifact of labor force re-entry after a shock, which is historically followed by a short-lived equity drawdown over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent in periods of stable labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumer spending momentum, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when savings are rising alongside strong income growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and a rise in CPIAUCSL (i.e., rates cut while inflation rises) signals a loss of central bank credibility, which erodes investor confidence and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed when inflation is falling.
